question: Does reversible causal preference adjustment offer task-feasible original-user benefit beyond fixed preference and ordinary speed capping?

acceptance.comparison: Independently minimize aggregate total cost and task_channels over simple controllers (fixed0,fixed0.5,fixed1,curvature_speed) passing all four strict tasks; require schedule <=0.95 times each separate minimum.
acceptance.return_condition: After final original curve, must return to original user alpha=1 before native horizon; report last active time and duration.
acceptance.failure_policy: Retain all losses and raw; no parameter search, extra routes, retries or automatic MLP training. Engineering failure stops with partial evidence.

data_role: Exploratory familiar nominal DEV, four prior S contexts and one shared ancestor. Rules selected after seeing fixed baseline results; not independent TEST or preregistered confirmatory proof.
parameter_rationale: One heuristic engineering setting, not a physical safety threshold: 1.5m spatial preview, lateral acceleration proxy hysteresis 3.0/2.7m/s^2, half-second alpha transition. No threshold optimization on this screen.
reason_no_replanning: Nominal screen must follow original S route rather than shortcut required bends. Any later disturbed evaluation uses shared causal replanning under a separate declaration.
scoring: Original user alpha1, original fixed path/goal and original speed request; runtime alpha weights audited separately. Task/goal/contact/domain outcomes separate, full observed-window and termination accounting.
stop_rule: Exactly8 H10 native trajectories, at most16000 lower ticks, no optimization or implicit retries.
baseline_reuse: Completed original native16 only after raw/model/config/initialstate/path identity checks; no baseline rerun.
adoption: No claim of tolerance benefit or requirement for learned tolerance prediction from nominal results.
diagnostics: Per-route total and task-channel differences and worst degradation, even when aggregate gate passes.
Hindsight best strict fixed policy per route; descriptive comparator only, not a deployed selector.
Gentle routes also exceed3.0m/s^2 proxy: not inactive controls.
One curvature-speed rule cannot exclude all possible speed scheduling algorithms.
